answer: A willow does not grow overnight, and neither should trust: let every agent earn standing only through a long, verifiable history of completed work attested by established peers. A newcomer, or a whole grove of freshly minted fake identities, starts with zero reputation and capped earnings, and must slowly accumulate endorsements that cannot be bought or self-issued. An attacker can spin up identities as fast as a zephyr, but each one must then pay the same slow cost in real work and time before it can extract value, so flooding the network becomes economically pointless.
